g.text: An Activity Diagram is a UML behavioral diagram that represents the flow of activities and control within a system. It illustrates the sequence
of actions from the initial node to the final node, including decision paths, branching, merging, and parallel execution (fork/join).
Each activity represents a task or operation, control flows specify execution order, and object flows trace data state transformations.
EXAMPLE WORKFLOW: E-Commerce Checkout & Order Fulfillment Process
CONTROL DYNAMICS: Starts at Initial Node → Validates via Decision Diamond → Splits via Fork Bar → Syncs at Join Bar → Ends at Final Node.
Key Components of an Activity Diagram
The nine foundational building blocks specified in UML behavioral standards

ARCHITECTURAL COMPARISON: ACTIVITY VS. STATE MACHINE & SEQUENCE DIAGRAMS
• Activity Diagram: Emphasizes computational workflows, parallel execution (fork/join), and data pipelines across a business process.
• State Machine / Sequence: Focuses on event-driven discrete state changes or chronological object message passing along lifelines.
